ws1_synthesis:
SCORING EFFICACY — KEEP/PRUNE RECOMMENDATION
(Gordon equities composite scorer; attribution n=37,405 baseline / 65,228 mean-reversion entered trades; 8 adversarial verifications)

==============================================================
1. COMPONENTS TO KEEP (robust, confirmed predictive)
==============================================================
NONE.

Zero components survive the full bar (sign-stable across regimes + survives composite_score/signal_strength confound controls + holds out-of-sample + economically non-trivial). Every component flagged "predictive" by per-slice attribution was independently REFUTED in adversarial verification:

- c_curve_total_range_20 (flagged predictive, baseline/Bullish): REFUTED — sign flips by regime (Bullish +0.067 / Bearish -0.082 / Neutral -0.094), partial-Spearman collapses to +0.005 (p=0.12) after controlling composite_score. Was proxying overall score.
- c_curve_net_direction_40 (flagged predictive, MR/ALL): REFUTED — effect is 100% Bearish; drop Bearish and r goes -0.039 → +0.001 (p=0.82). |r|~0.04.
- c_trend (flagged predictive, MR/ALL): REFUTED — survives confounds but sign-unstable (Bearish -0.065 vs Bullish +0.010), single-regime, Q1→Q5 spread only ~0.4pp.
- c_curve_total_range_40 (flagged predictive, MR/ALL): REFUTED — survives confounds but 2 of 5 walk-forward folds flip positive; 70/30 temporal split kills it (OOS r=-0.005, p=0.50).
- c_volume / c_curve_net_direction_20 (flagged predictive, MR/Bullish): REFUTED — both sign-flip across regimes and collapse to NS under composite_score control.

==============================================================
2. PRUNE (noise) and FLIP/INVESTIGATE (anti)
==============================================================
PRUNE — statistical noise, no rank power over forward PnL (carry no weight or trivial weight). Across all 8 slices these never cleared monotonicity + confound + OOS together:
c_candlestick, c_momentum, c_moving_average, c_price_action, c_rs_index, c_intraday_context, c_intraday_resistance, c_limit, c_penalty_rsi, c_penalty_ema_overextension, c_penalty_volume_exhaustion, c_bonus_oversold_rsi, c_bonus_oversold_bb, c_bonus_selling_climax, c_mean_reversion_specific, c_curve, c_curve_motif_score_20, c_curve_motif_score_40.

Note the named "edge" bonuses are dead: c_bonus_oversold_rsi/bb and c_mean_reversion_specific are statistical noise (|t|<1 in the MR/ALL slice) — the mean-reversion strategy's signature inputs add nothing.

FLIP/INVESTIGATE — anti-signals (higher score → WORSE return), confirmed monotonic but ALL regime-confined to Bearish:
- c_volume — the ONLY component whose anti sign is stable across all baseline regimes (Bearish -0.052 / Bullish -0.017 / Neutral -0.041) AND survives confound controls (baseline/ALL r=-0.011 p=0.047; Bearish r=-0.041 p=0.0001). Real but economically tiny (Q5-Q1 spread -0.2 to -0.45pp). Strongest candidate for a sign flip or zero-weight.
- c_moving_average / c_trend / c_curve_total_range_20/40 / c_curve_net_direction_20/40 — flagged anti in Bearish, but every one is single-regime (Bearish-only), sign-flips in Bullish, and/or fails OOS. Do NOT flip blindly; the inversion is "trend/up-curve scores fade in falling markets," i.e. the trend-following scorer is mis-calibrated for shorting — not a tradable standalone anti-signal. Investigate as a regime gate, not a weight flip.

==============================================================
3. HEADLINE VERDICT
==============================================================
The composite_score has NO usable, durable edge over realized forward PnL among already-entered trades. Max |IC| anywhere is ~0.046 (curve-motif family) and even that fails monotonicity; the largest |IC| values (~0.15 in baseline/Bearish) are regime-composition artifacts that cancel pooled (overall Spearman ≈ 0, p=0.94). Every "predictive" flag was refuted under sign-stability + confound + OOS testing. The one robust finding is negative: c_volume is a mild ANTI-signal in baseline. Practical read — the scorer ranks entered candidates essentially at random with respect to their post-entry return; its only demonstrable bias (volume) is counterproductive.

Important scope caveat: this measures rank power AMONG ENTERED trades, i.e. residual edge after the entry filter. It does NOT prove the score is worthless as an entry gate (selection effect is invisible here). The claim is narrow: it adds no usable information for sizing/ranking among the trades it already selected.

==============================================================
4. SINGLE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE CHANGE
==============================================================
Stop using composite_score as a position-sizing / ranking signal among entered candidates — size uniformly (or by an external risk model), since the score's rank order is uninformative-to-counterproductive over forward PnL. Coupled lever: zero out or invert c_volume's contribution in the baseline scorer (it is the one stable, confound-surviving, monotonic relationship and it points the wrong way). This is the only change backed by a finding that survived all three robustness gates.

(Do NOT chase the Bearish-regime anti-signals into weight flips — they are single-regime and OOS-unstable. If anything, the Bearish findings argue for a regime gate that suppresses or inverts trend-following scoring in Bearish regimes, which is a research task, not a weight tweak.)

==============================================================
5. CAVEATS
==============================================================
- HYPOTHETICAL, NOT LIVE: This is backtest/attribution evidence on entered-trade outcomes, not realized broker P&L. No live capital validated any of this.
- SELECTION EFFECT: Analysis is conditional on entry — it cannot speak to the score's value as the entry filter itself (the most likely place any real edge lives).
- REGIME CONCENTRATION: Nearly every significant relationship lives entirely in the Bearish subsample (the smallest, most negative-PnL regime: baseline n=10,892 mean -0.22%; MR n=28,619 mean -0.46%). Bearish is where the strategy loses money, so "signal" there is largely "the scorer mis-reads falling markets," not exploitable alpha.
- SAMPLE / MULTIPLICITY: Large n inflates t-stats — several |t|>3 components are statistically significant yet economically trivial (|IC|<0.05, R²<0.2%, Q5-Q1 spreads ~0.2-0.8pp) and fail monotonicity. The monotonicity + OOS + confound gates (not raw t) are doing the real work.
- ECONOMIC TRIVIALITY: Even the "surviving" anti-relationships move forward PnL by tenths of a percentage point per quintile — below plausible transaction-cost noise.
- MR STRATEGY IS NET-LOSING in this dataset (43.0% WR, -0.17% mean PnL), so its component attribution is partly explaining a losing process; "anti" there is not symmetric to tradable short alpha.
- Neutral slices are small (baseline n=2,072; MR n=4,908) and the most profitable — but yield zero confirmed signal, so high win-rate there is not attributable to the scorer.

ws4_methods.method: Mark Minervini SEPA (Specific Entry Point Analysis) / VCP (Volatility Contraction Pattern)
ws4_methods.core_idea: SEPA is a trend-following, buy-strength growth methodology built on "Stage 2" uptrends (Stan Weinstein stage analysis). The thesis: leading stocks under heavy institutional accumulation form a recognizable base where each successive pullback gets shallower and volume dries up (the VCP), signaling sellers are exhausted. You buy the breakout out of that final, tightest contraction with a precise, tight stop, riding the established uptrend. SEPA is the full filter (trend + fundamentals + relative strength + catalyst + VCP shape); VCP is the price/volume entry pattern within it. Minervini's edge is asymmetry: tight stops at the pivot keep losers small while winners run, so a sub-50% win rate is profitable.
ws4_methods.selection: Practitioners run a multi-gate funnel. (1) Trend Template (8 rules on daily price vs MAs): price > 150-day and 200-day SMA; 150-day > 200-day; 200-day trending up >=1 month; 50-day > both 150 and 200; price > 50-day; price >=30% above its 52-week low; price within ~25% of its 52-week high; and high Relative Strength rank (IBD RS >= 70, ideally 80-90+) measuring the stock's price performance vs the whole market. This isolates Stage-2 leaders. (2) Fundamental overlay (SEPA): accelerating EPS/sales growth, margin expansion, institutional sponsorship, a catalyst — the "code 33"/leadership screen. (3) VCP shape: a base of 2-6 progressively tighter contractions (e.g. 25% -> 15% -> 8% pullbacks), each on diminishing volume, with a final tight "cheat"/pivot and volume dry-up (lowest volume days near the apex). The pivot/buy-point is the high of the final contraction.
ws4_methods.entry: Buy a breakout through the pivot price (top of the final, tightest contraction) on a surge of volume — practitioners want volume well above average (often 1.5x+ the 50-day avg) confirming demand. Entry is intraday as price clears the pivot, often using a buy-stop limit just above the pivot to avoid chasing. Position is added only in the lowest-risk window where the stop can be kept tight (typically risk to stop is held to ~1.25-2.5% on the position, scaling size to keep portfolio risk ~0.5-1.25% per trade). The defining feature is the precision of the entry point, not a daily-close signal.
ws4_methods.exit: Initial stop placed just below the breakout pivot / low of the final contraction, sized so the loss is small (Minervini caps individual losses, averages well under his average gain to keep batting-average tolerance). On the way up: sell into strength on climax/exhaustion moves, raise stop to breakeven after the trade gains ~the initial risk, then trail using the 50-day (or sometimes 21-day EMA for fast movers) — exit on a decisive break of the moving-average trail or a violation of the prior swing low. Hold horizon is open-ended (weeks to many months for a true Stage-2 runner); there is no fixed time-stop. Win rate is intentionally modest (often 40-50%) with a >2:1 average-win-to-average-loss ratio.
ws4_methods.how_to_test_here: Build a SEPA-VCP-lite as a new TradingStrategy subclass (strategy_interface.py + strategy_registry.py — the pluggable interface means zero downstream churn). SELECTION on daily bars only: implement the 8-rule Trend Template using existing MA indicators (add 150-day SMA alongside 50/200; we already have crossovers and a 52-week-high scorer in limit_indicators.score_52_week_range) plus a synthetic Relative Strength rank computed cross-sectionally over the 11k-symbol DuckDB universe (rolling 63/126/252-day return percentile vs all symbols on each date — this is pure price data, no fundamentals needed). VCP SHAPE on daily bars: detect 2-4 successive swing-high-to-low contractions with monotonically shrinking depth and falling volume using ATR/Donchian-channel width compression (volatility contraction = N-day ATR or high-low range now < prior contraction) + a volume-dry-up gate (recent 5-day vol < base-period avg). Define the pivot = base high; ENTRY = next-day open/breakout above pivot on >1.5x avg volume; STOP = base low / pivot - k*ATR; satisfies min RR>1.0. Then run it through trade_evaluator.py / hypothesis_engine.py over the DuckDB 1999-present store. KEY ADAPTATION: our 5-10 day bracket horizon contradicts SEPA's open-ended trail, so test a bracketized variant (fixed target = pivot + R-multiple, ATR trail, 10-day time-stop) and measure whether the VCP+RS selection still has positive expectancy when forced into a short hold. Gate via the hypothetical-trade evaluator's expectancy CI as we did for the forex v2 cells.

ws4_methods.method: William O'Neil CAN SLIM (growth-stock breakout system from "How to Make Money in Stocks")
ws4_methods.core_idea: CAN SLIM is a hybrid fundamental+technical growth system that buys market-leading companies at the moment institutional demand overwhelms supply. The acronym is the seven-leg selection filter: C = current quarterly EPS up >=25% YoY (accelerating); A = annual EPS growth >=25% over 3+ years with high ROE; N = a New driver (product, management, or new price high breaking from a base); S = Supply/demand, i.e. price breakout confirmed by volume >=40-50% above average and tight supply; L = Leader not laggard, operationalized as Relative Strength rank (price vs the market) in the top ~20-30% (RS>=80); I = increasing Institutional sponsorship by quality funds; M = Market direction (only buy in a confirmed uptrend, follow distribution-day counts on SPX/Nasdaq). It is a long-only, trend/momentum-on-leaders philosophy: ride strength, not reversion.
ws4_methods.selection: Practitioners screen the fundamental gate first (C/A: >=25% quarterly & annual EPS growth, high ROE; I: rising fund ownership), then require L: Relative Strength line at new high and RS rank >=80-87, then require M: general market in a confirmed uptrend (the buy switch is OFF in corrections/distribution). Among survivors they look for a chart base: cup-with-handle (classic, >=7 weeks, 12-33% cup depth, shallow handle in the upper half), flat base, double-bottom, or high-tight flag. The 'pivot point' is the buy trigger price = handle high (or base resistance) plus ~$0.10.
ws4_methods.entry: Buy as price breaks ABOVE the pivot (handle/base high) intraday, only within the first ~5% above the pivot ('buy zone' = pivot to pivot+5%; chasing beyond 5% is forbidden as 'extended'). The breakout MUST be confirmed by volume at least 40-50% above the 50-day average that day. No fundamentals/RS confirmation re-checked at entry; the base + volume surge IS the entry signal. Pyramid adds are allowed as the position works, but the initial bracket is the breakout bar.
ws4_methods.exit: Hard stop: sell if price falls 7-8% below the purchase (pivot) price, no exceptions ('cut every loss at 8%'). Profit: take most gains in the 20-25% range above the pivot. Key exception: if a stock gains >=20% within the first 1-3 weeks of breakout, HOLD it at least 8 weeks (treat as a potential big winner). Sell signals also fire on technical breakdown (close below 50-day MA on heavy volume, climax top, biggest one-day drop). Holding period is weeks-to-months for winners, not a fixed bar count.
ws4_methods.how_to_test_here: Build a TECHNICAL-ONLY CAN SLIM proxy on our DuckDB OHLCV (1999-present, ~11k symbols) and run it through the hypothetical-trade evaluator. Implement the three codable legs: (1) S/N = base+breakout detector on daily bars: detect a >=7-week base (rolling 35-bar consolidation, depth 12-33% off interior high), define pivot = base high, fire a long when close>pivot AND today's volume>=1.4x the 50-day avg volume; restrict fills to within 5% above pivot. (2) L = relative strength: reuse the existing RS indicator (RS_MULTIPLIER in weights.json) — require RS-rank >=80th percentile vs the universe (or vs SPY) on the breakout date. (3) M = market regime: gate entries to MarketRegime bullish on SPY/QQQ (already advisory in market_regime.py); reject in distribution. Bracket: entry=pivot+0.1%, stop=entry*0.925 (7.5%), target=entry*1.225 (22.5%) — that is 3:1 R:R, well above our >1.0 floor. Run two horizon variants to bridge the mismatch: (a) our standard 5-10 day MAX_HOLD timeout, and (b) a relaxed 40-bar hold to honor O'Neil's let-winners-run rule, and compare win-rate / mean-R / expectancy across regimes. Apply our standard filters ($5-$500, >100k vol). Leave C/A/I/N-fundamental legs OUT and label the result a 'CAN SLIM technical proxy' — flag that the fundamental gate is the documented source of most of the edge and is unmeasured here.

ws4_methods.method: Stan Weinstein Stage Analysis (weekly Stage 2 breakouts)
ws4_methods.core_idea: Classify every stock into one of four stages defined by its 30-week (150-day) moving average: Stage 1 = basing/accumulation (price oscillating around a flat 30-wk MA after a decline); Stage 2 = advancing (price breaks above the base on expanding volume and rides a RISING 30-wk MA upward); Stage 3 = topping/distribution (30-wk MA flattens, price chops); Stage 4 = declining (price below a falling 30-wk MA). The entire edge is: only own stocks in Stage 2, get in at the Stage 2A breakout (transition from Stage 1 to 2), and hold the trend until it demonstrably ends. It is a weekly-chart, trend-following methodology, not a short-hold swing method.
ws4_methods.selection: Practitioners scan weekly charts for stocks whose price is breaking ABOVE a multi-month horizontal base (the Stage 1 platform), where (1) the 30-week MA has flattened and is just beginning to turn up, (2) price closes above both the resistance/pivot line of the base and the 30-week MA, (3) the breakout occurs on volume 2-3x the average (volume confirmation is mandatory — a breakout on weak volume is suspect/false), and (4) Mansfield Relative Strength (the stock's price vs. a market index, plotted as a zero-line oscillator) is positive and rising, i.e. the stock is outperforming the broad market. Candidates with the tightest, longest bases and the strongest RS are preferred. Weinstein also overlays overall market posture: he wants the major averages themselves in Stage 2 before committing aggressively.
ws4_methods.entry: Buy on the breakout: either (a) the aggressive entry as price closes through the base's resistance line on heavy volume, or (b) the conservative entry on the first low-volume pullback toward the breakout level / the rising 30-week MA (a 'buy the throwback' add). The pivot is the top of the base. Continuation entries (Stage 2 'continuation breakouts' out of mid-trend consolidations) use the same rule on each new base.
ws4_methods.exit: Exits are trend-based and slow, not a fixed bracket. Initial protective stop goes just below the breakout pivot or below the most recent higher-low. As the trade works, the stop is trailed up under successive higher-lows / under the rising 30-week MA. The position is SOLD when the stock transitions out of Stage 2: price breaks decisively below the 30-week MA AND/OR the 30-week MA itself flattens and rolls over (Stage 3->4). Typical holding period is many weeks to several months — Weinstein explicitly rides intermediate-to-major trends, not 5-10 day moves.
ws4_methods.how_to_test_here: All selection inputs are computable in our daily DuckDB stack: approximate the 30-week MA with a 150-day SMA (we already have WMA/VWMA/SMA in moving_average_indicators.py); detect the base breakout with calculate_donchian (close > prior N-day Donchian upper, e.g. 50-100 day) plus a flat-then-rising 150-day MA slope filter; require volume confirmation via calculate_rvol (>= 2x 20-day avg) which is already wired; build Mansfield RS as a new feature = (close / SPY_close) normalized vs its own 52-week range, computed from the DuckDB SPY series; gate on market regime (market_regime.py SPY/QQQ EMA health) for the 'major averages in Stage 2' condition. Encode this as a TradingStrategy subclass (per MEMORY: subclass TradingStrategy, register in strategy_registry.py, zero downstream changes) emitting entry=breakout close, stop=below pivot/recent higher-low (cap at MAX_RISK_PERCENT 5%), target=R-multiple to keep RR>1.0. Then test TWO ways with Backtester: (1) FAITHFUL — set hold_days long (e.g. 60-120), use_trailing_stop=True with a wide trailing_multiplier and a 150-day-MA-break exit, to measure the method as designed; (2) TRUNCATED — clamp hold_days=5-10 with a fixed bracket to measure whether the Stage-2 breakout SIGNAL still has edge inside our actual horizon. Compare both via the hypothetical-trade evaluator / journal across the 1999-present, ~11k-symbol store, slicing by market-regime bucket since Weinstein's edge is regime-dependent.

ws4_methods.method: Nicolas Darvas Box Theory (trend-following breakout from consolidation boxes)
ws4_methods.core_idea: Strong stocks rise in a stair-step pattern: a sharp advance, then a consolidation range (a "box"), then another advance. Darvas tracked stocks making new highs, waited for them to pause inside a tight box defined by price action, and bought the breakout above the box top with volume confirmation. He rode the trend by trailing his stop up the bottom of each successive higher box, and exited only when price broke back below the current box. The edge is pure momentum/trend-continuation plus disciplined, structure-based risk control.
ws4_methods.selection: Practitioners screen for: (1) stocks at/near new highs — classically 52-week highs; (2) strong volume on the advance (Darvas wanted accelerating volume, breakout volume often >=150% of average); (3) leadership in a strong industry group / high relative strength sector. Darvas explicitly avoided sideways or declining markets and weak groups. He traded a narrow watchlist of the strongest names rather than a broad screen.
ws4_methods.entry: Box construction (classic 3-day rule): after a new high is set, if 3 consecutive sessions fail to exceed that high, the high becomes the BOX TOP. The subsequent low that then holds for 3 consecutive sessions (not breached) becomes the BOX BOTTOM. Entry = a buy-stop a few ticks/points ABOVE the box top, triggered only when price decisively breaks out (not a marginal tick over), ideally on a volume surge. Marginal pokes above the high are explicitly rejected.
ws4_methods.exit: Initial stop just BELOW the box bottom (structural support; a break means the breakout failed). The stop is trailed upward: each time a new, higher box forms above the entry box, the stop is raised to the new box's bottom — a structure-based trailing stop requiring no discretion. Profitable exit is open-ended: hold while price keeps making higher boxes; exit only when price breaks below the current (highest confirmed) box. Pyramiding: add to the position on each new box breakout.
ws4_methods.how_to_test_here: All inputs exist on the stack: rolling-max / Donchian / new-high primitives already live in trend_indicators.py and price_action_indicators.py; volume indicators (RVOL) exist in volume_indicators.py; SPY/QQQ regime is wired and advisory. Plan: (1) Implement a DarvasBox indicator in price_action_indicators.py that, per bar, tracks state: detect a fresh N-day high (parameterize new-high window: 52-week=252d vs a shorter 60-90d swing variant), confirm box top after 3 bars fail to exceed it, confirm box bottom after 3 bars hold above the post-top low. Emit box_top, box_bottom, and a breakout flag (close or intraday-high > box_top by a small buffer, with RVOL>=1.5 gate). (2) Map to our bracket: entry = box_top + buffer; stop = box_bottom (compute risk% = (entry-stop)/entry, reject if >MAX_RISK_PERCENT=5%); target = entry + RR*(entry-stop) with RR sized so min R:R>1.0 — pick a fixed target (e.g. 2R) OR a Darvas-faithful trailing variant. (3) Backtest via Backtester.run_backtest over the DuckDB store (1999-present, ~11k symbols), using --strategy as a new registered strategy (subclass TradingStrategy per strategy_interface.py, register in strategy_registry.py — picklable for ProcessPool). Two backtest configs to compare: (a) fixed bracket capped at MAX_HOLD 10 days (honors our horizon), (b) box-trailing stop with no fixed target but a 10-day max-hold cap (closest faithful version our evaluator allows). Apply price ($5-$500) and volume (>100k) filters already in the pipeline. (4) Measure mean R, win rate, R:R distribution, and hold-length histogram via the hypothetical-trade evaluator; regime-split by SPY trend since Darvas only works in uptrending markets. Faithful Darvas is the trickiest part to honor under a fixed 5-10d horizon — the box-trail config (b) is the honest test of whether truncating the let-it-run tail kills the edge.

ws4_methods.method: Larry Connors RSI(2) / short-term mean reversion (Street Smarts 1996; Short Term Trading Strategies That Work, 2008)
ws4_methods.core_idea: Buy short-term panic, sell short-term euphoria, but only in the direction of the long-term trend. A 2-period RSI is hypersensitive and spikes to extremes after just 1-3 bars of directional movement; Connors/Alvarez found that the lower the RSI(2) dips, the higher the forward returns. The edge is a 1-5 day snapback toward the mean, not a multi-week swing. Backtests on indices/large caps showed 65-85% win rates with small per-trade gains.
ws4_methods.selection: Daily bars. Two-gate long screen: (1) TREND FILTER: Close > 200-day SMA (only buy oversold dips inside an uptrend). (2) TRIGGER: 2-period RSI(close) < 10, with the canonical refinement that RSI(2) < 5 gives a stronger edge than < 10 (monotonic: lower = better). Optional extra layers practitioners add: price also below 5-SMA, and a "cumulative RSI(2) over 2 days < 35" variant (ConnorsRSI lineage) to require persistence. Shorts are the mirror (Close < 200-SMA AND RSI(2) > 90) but Connors himself noted long mean-reversion is the robust side on US equities. No fundamentals, no volume gate in the original (he traded liquid indices/large caps, so volume was implicit).
ws4_methods.entry: Enter long at the close of the signal bar (Connors' tests assume MOC fill) or, as practitioners commonly implement it, at next day's open. Position sizing is flat/equal-weight; he scaled in on deeper dips (add a second unit if RSI(2) stays < 10 the next day) but the simple version is single-unit market entry.
ws4_methods.exit: CONDITION-BASED, not a fixed bracket. Primary exit: close the long when Close > 5-day SMA (the snapback completed). Alternate published exit: RSI(2) > 70 (or > 65). Critically, Connors EXPLICITLY recommends NO hard stop-loss — his testing on stocks/indices found fixed stops degraded expectancy because they convert temporary drawdown into realized losses right before the mean-reversion fires. Hold is open-ended but empirically resolves in ~1-5 trading days; if the trend filter breaks (Close < 200-SMA) the trade is also exited.
ws4_methods.how_to_test_here: All ingredients exist in-stack. (1) Add an `rsi_2` computation: TA-Lib RSI timeperiod=2 in `momentum_indicators.py` (our current `calculate_rsi` is 14-period and bucket-scored, so add a raw RSI(2) value, do not reuse the scorer). Add a 200-SMA and 5-SMA pull from the DuckDB OHLCV store. (2) Selection as a screen over the DuckDB universe (1999-present, ~11k symbols): filter price $5-$500, 20d avg volume >100k, Close>SMA200, RSI(2)<10 (and a separate <5 arm). (3) Map to our bracket via `trade_evaluator.py` (`TradeEvalConfig`/`evaluate_bars`): entry = next-day open; this is where the methodology must be ADAPTED — to honor our hard constraints, set a stop (e.g. entry - 1.0*ATR or recent swing low) and a target sized for RR>1.0, with `hold_days` capped at 5-10. Run TWO arms: (A) Connors-faithful = no stop / exit on Close>5-SMA (requires a tiny custom exit branch in the evaluator, the closest to his real edge) vs (B) our-constraint-faithful = fixed ATR bracket + hold cap. (4) Use the hypothetical-trade evaluator / `Backtester.run_backtest` to get per-trade R, win rate, mean R with CI (apply the V2 expectancy gate mean_R - 1.96*SE > 0), and compare arm A vs B. Sweep RSI threshold {5,10}, exit {5-SMA, RSI(2)>70, fixed RR}, hold cap {3,5,7,10}. Decision metric per your THROUGHPUT preference: $/day-per-slot and P(hit goal), not just per-trade R, since RSI(2) trades resolve fast and cycle slots quickly.

ws4_methods.core_idea: Bollinger Bands plot a 20-period SMA (middle band) with upper/lower bands at +/-2 standard deviations. %b normalizes price within the bands: %b = (close - lower) / (upper - lower), so 0 = on the lower band, 0.5 = at the SMA, 1.0 = on the upper band. The mean-reversion thesis is that price stretched to the lower band (low/negative %b) is statistically over-extended and tends to revert toward the SMA. Practitioners do NOT buy a simple lower-band touch (price can ride the band down in a strong trend); they wait for a REVERSAL confirmation: price pierces below the lower band (%b < 0 or <= 0.05) and then closes back inside the band (%b crosses up through 0), ideally on a bullish candle (hammer/engulfing) and with an oscillator confirming oversold (RSI(2-3) low, %R < -80, or a 'W-bottom' where the second low holds above the first with higher %b = bullish divergence). Bandwidth = (upper-lower)/middle is often used as a regime filter (avoid buying dips while bands are violently expanding -- a 'walking the band' downtrend). The edge is a short-term snap-back, not a trend.
ws4_methods.selection: Universe scan for names where the prior bar's close was below (or touched) the lower Bollinger Band (20,2) and the most recent bar closes back inside the band -- i.e. %b crossed from <=0 up through 0. Rank/filter the candidates by confirmation strength: oversold oscillator (RSI(2) or RSI(3) very low, Connors RSI < 20, %R < -80, z-score < -2), a bullish reversal candle on the cross bar, and optionally bullish %b divergence (W-bottom). Many practitioners add a long-term trend gate (price above 200-SMA) so they only buy dips in names that are structurally uptrending, and a bandwidth/regime filter to skip violent expansions. This is a screen producing a handful of long candidates per day, not a single-symbol system.
ws4_methods.entry: Enter long at/after the bar that closes back inside the lower band (%b > 0). Practitioner variants: (a) market-on-open the next session, or (b) a stop-entry above the confirmation bar's high to require follow-through, or (c) a limit at/near the prior close. For our bracket model, the natural mapping is: signal on bar T (the close-back-inside bar), enter next session (T+1) at open or via a limit near the signal close.
ws4_methods.exit: Canonical exit is a PROFIT TARGET at the middle band (the 20-SMA) -- a 'walk to the mean' -- which is a moving target, not a fixed price. Aggressive variants target the upper band. Stop is placed just below the reversal-bar low or the recent swing low (often 1-1.5 ATR), since a clean failure of the reversal invalidates the setup. Time stop: classic BB reversion is fast (typically 2-6 bars to tag the SMA); positions are commonly exited if the mean isn't reached within ~5-10 bars. So the live rule set is: target = middle band (dynamic) OR fixed R-multiple, stop = below reversal low, plus a time exit.
ws4_methods.how_to_test_here: Everything needed is already on the stack -- this is a parameterization/screen, not new infra. (1) BB(20,2) is already computed in src/bluehorseshoe/data/historical_data.py:610 (ta.BBANDS, nbdevup/dn=2), persisted as bb_upper/bb_middle/bb_lower in DuckDB ohlcv.duckdb. (2) A %b-style scorer already exists: calculate_bb_position() in src/bluehorseshoe/analysis/indicators/momentum_indicators.py:156 -- but it is the WRONG SHAPE for this method (it rewards mid-band 0.3-0.7 and only penalizes >0.85; it never rewards the <0 -> cross-up reversal). To test the methodology faithfully, add a lower-band-reversal sub-indicator alongside the existing mean-reversion suite in src/bluehorseshoe/analysis/indicators/mean_reversion_indicators.py (which already houses z-score, Connors RSI, DV2 -- the natural confirmation oscillators). (3) Build the candidate set by either driving the existing MeanReversionStrategy with a %b-cross gate, or computing the signal directly off DuckDB. (4) Backtest with src/bluehorseshoe/analysis/backtest.py (Backtester / BacktestConfig already supports target_profit_factor, stop_loss_factor, hold_days, use_trailing_stop) -- run ./run.sh python src/main.py -t with --strategy mean_reversion over a date range, and sweep hold_days ~ 5-10 and an R:R-positive target/stop. (5) The dynamic 'exit at middle band' target is NOT representable by the fixed-factor bracket; test it via the hypothetical-trade evaluator (src/bluehorseshoe/analysis/trade_evaluator.py + hypothesis_engine.py) or extend Backtester with a 'middle-band target' exit so you can compare fixed-R bracket vs walk-to-mean. (6) Add the 200-SMA trend gate and a SPY/QQQ regime gate (market_regime.py, advisory) as ablations. Measure win-rate, mean R, and time-to-target distribution on the DuckDB 1999-present, ~11k symbol store with the $5-$500 / >100k-volume filters already in constants.py.

ws4_methods.method: Dual-momentum / relative-strength rotation (Gary Antonacci, "Dual Momentum Investing"; canonical implementation = GEM, Global Equities Momentum).
ws4_methods.core_idea: Combine two momentum filters to decide WHAT to hold each month. (1) RELATIVE momentum: rank a small set of assets by trailing total return (canonically 12-month) and prefer the strongest. (2) ABSOLUTE momentum (a.k.a. time-series momentum / trend filter): the chosen risky asset must also beat the risk-free rate (T-bill / cash) over the same 12-month window; if it does not, the entire allocation moves to bonds (AGG). The synergy claim: relative momentum picks the leader, absolute momentum is a crash-protection regime switch that exits risk entirely in bear markets. It is an asset-allocation rotation method, NOT a single-name swing system.
ws4_methods.selection: Practitioners run it on a tiny universe of broad indices/ETFs, not individual stocks. Canonical GEM = 3 assets: US equities (SPY/VOO), ex-US developed equities (VEU/ACWX), aggregate bonds (AGG/BND). Monthly, on the last trading day: compute trailing 12-month total return for SPY and the risk-free rate (e.g. BIL / 1-3mo T-bill). If SPY 12m return > T-bill return (absolute momentum PASS): hold whichever of SPY vs ex-US has the higher 12m return (relative momentum winner). If SPY 12m return <= T-bill (FAIL): hold AGG. Sector/factor variants (e.g. dual-momentum sector rotation) expand the universe to ~10 sector ETFs, rank by 12m (sometimes blended 3/6/12m) momentum, hold the top 1-3, but keep the same absolute-momentum cash/bond escape hatch. Lookback is almost always 6-12 months; 12m has the most out-of-sample support.
ws4_methods.entry: Discrete monthly rebalance: enter the selected asset at the close of the last trading day of the month (or next-day open). No intra-month entries, no per-trade price triggers. Entry is "be 100% in asset X for the coming month," determined purely by the cross-sectional momentum ranking plus the absolute-momentum gate.
ws4_methods.exit: No price-based stop or profit target. The exit IS the next monthly evaluation: you hold the position for the full month, then re-rank. You rotate out only when (a) another asset outranks the current holding on relative momentum, or (b) the absolute-momentum filter flips to FAIL and you move to bonds/cash. Average holding period is months-to-quarters; turnover is deliberately low (1-2 trades/year in pure GEM).
ws4_methods.how_to_test_here: Direct port is impossible: GEM has no entry/stop/target bracket and no 5-10d horizon — its native unit is a monthly all-in allocation across ~3 ETFs, while our backtester (src/bluehorseshoe/analysis/backtest.py) takes per-symbol {entry_price, stop_loss, take_profit} with a hold_days cap (default 3) and RR>1.0 gate. The only honest test on our stack is to extract the TRANSFERABLE PRIMITIVES, not the strategy: (1) Use the DuckDB store (1999-present) to compute a 12m (252-bar) ROC relative-strength rank across our long universe; treat it as a NEW candidate-selection FILTER feeding the existing hypothetical-trade evaluator — i.e. only allow long swing entries on names in the top RS decile, with our normal ATR-based stop/target bracket and 5-10d hold. (2) Implement the absolute-momentum gate as a REGIME overlay in market_regime.py: require SPY's trailing 12m return > 0 (or > T-bill proxy) before allowing any long swing entries — this is a clean, additive bolt-on that fits our SPY/QQQ regime inputs. (3) A/B the hypothetical-trade evaluator with vs without each overlay (RS-rank filter; absolute-momentum regime gate; both) over 1999-present to measure win-rate / mean-R lift. We CANNOT meaningfully backtest GEM-the-rotation here because we have no multi-asset portfolio allocator, no ex-US/bond instruments in scope (long US equities only), and no monthly-rebalance accounting. Avoid: trying to shoehorn a monthly hold into hold_days, or running it on single names with brackets — that is no longer Antonacci's method and tests nothing he validated.

ws4_methods.method: 52-Week-High / Time-Series Momentum (two related academic methods). (1) Cross-sectional 52-week-high momentum — George & Hwang (2004), "The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing": rank stocks by NEARNESS to their trailing 52-week high, defined as the ratio FH = current_price / max(high over past 252 trading days). Buy the highest-FH decile (price hugging its 52wk high), short the lowest. Behavioral basis: the 52wk high is a psychological anchor — traders under-react to good news that pushes price toward the anchor, so prices that are already near the high continue upward. George-Hwang showed FH-nearness dominates and subsumes Jegadeesh-Titman past-return momentum, and (unlike JT momentum) its profits do NOT reverse long-run. (2) Time-Series momentum — Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), "Time Series Momentum": an absolute (own-history, not cross-sectional) rule — if an instrument's trailing 12-month excess return is POSITIVE, go long; if negative, go short. Position sized inversely to recent realized volatility (vol-scaling to a target, e.g. 40% annualized). 12-month lookback, ~1-month hold, monthly rebalance. Effect persists ~12 months then partially reverses. Both are calendar-rebalanced ranking/sign systems, not intraday signals.
ws4_methods.core_idea: Stocks/instruments that are already strong continue to be strong over the next ~1-12 months. The "tell" is either nearness to the trailing 1-year high (52WH, an anchoring proxy) or the sign of the trailing 12-month return (TSMOM). Momentum is a slow, low-turnover, long-horizon edge driven by under-reaction; it is a portfolio/ranking discipline, not a swing trigger.
ws4_methods.selection: 52WH variant: rank the long-eligible universe by FH = last_close / rolling_252d_high; take the top decile (or top-N, FH typically >0.95). TSMOM variant: keep only instruments whose trailing 252-day total return is positive (sign filter), then equal-risk weight. Both rebalance monthly on a fixed calendar, and both rank/filter on a long lookback (252 trading days). Neither selects on a same-day chart pattern.
ws4_methods.entry: Calendar-driven, at the rebalance date, entered at the next open/close — NOT a price-conditional bracket. There is no per-name entry trigger, stop, or limit price; you simply hold the selected basket. (TSMOM additionally vol-targets the per-name notional.) This is the single biggest divergence from our entry/stop/target bracket model.
ws4_methods.exit: Calendar exit at the next monthly rebalance (typical 1-month hold for TSMOM; 6-12 month holding-period studies for 52WH, often with overlapping portfolios). Exit is "name fell out of the top decile / 12m return flipped negative," not a profit target or stop-loss. No risk:reward bracket; risk is managed at the portfolio level via diversification and (TSMOM) vol-scaling.
ws4_methods.how_to_test_here: The signal computation fits cleanly; the trade STRUCTURE does not, so test the SIGNAL as a feature/scorer, not the published portfolio rule. Concretely: (1) Add a `calculate_52wk_high_nearness()` indicator beside `calculate_donchian()` in `src/bluehorseshoe/analysis/indicators/trend_indicators.py` — FH = close / data['high'].rolling(252).max() (Donchian at window=252 is already 90% of this; reuse that machinery and register a `FH52W_MULTIPLIER` in weights.json). The repo already computes a 52-period rolling high in `calculate_ichimoku` (spanB), so the primitive exists. (2) Stand up a new `Strategy52WHMomentum(TradingStrategy)` subclass via the pluggable interface in `src/bluehorseshoe/analysis/strategy_interface.py` + register in `strategy_registry.py` (per MEMORY: subclass + register = zero downstream changes). ws4_methods.method: Turtle / Donchian channel breakout (Dennis & Eckhardt Turtle System 1 and 2)
ws4_methods.core_idea: A volatility-normalized trend-following breakout system. The thesis: prices that break out of their recent N-day range tend to keep moving in the breakout direction often enough that a few large winners pay for many small losers. Donchian channels (rolling N-day highest-high / lowest-low) define the range; the breakout is the entry trigger. Edge comes from (1) catching the rare sustained trend, (2) cutting losers fast at a fixed ATR-based stop, and (3) letting winners run open-endedly while pyramiding the position. It is NOT a high-win-rate system — typical win rate is 30-45% and the entire expectancy lives in the right tail of trade duration.
ws4_methods.selection: No ranking/scoring screen in the original. The Turtles traded a fixed, hand-picked universe of liquid futures (currencies, bonds, metals, energy, grains, softs) and took EVERY qualifying breakout in that universe, sizing each by volatility. 'Selection' is really universe construction + a liquidity filter, not a top-N candidate list. Practitioners adapting it to equities typically: (a) restrict to liquid, optionable, high-dollar-volume names; (b) optionally add a long-term trend filter (e.g., price > 200-day MA, or a 50/100-day channel context) so they only take longs in uptrends; (c) take all breakouts that pass, capped by total portfolio heat (sum of open-trade risk), not by a per-day candidate count. The two canonical entry channels: System 1 = 20-day high; System 2 = 55-day high. System 1 has a 'last-breakout filter' (skip a 20-day breakout if the prior breakout was a winner, to avoid chopping; if skipped, the 55-day System-2 breakout still fires as a safety net).
ws4_methods.entry: Long: buy a stop order placed at (or 1 tick beyond) the highest high of the prior N days (N=20 for System 1, 55 for System 2). The breakout is intrabar — original Turtles entered the moment price traded through the level, NOT on close. Position sizing: 1 'Unit' = (1% of account equity) / (N x dollars-per-point), where N = the 20-day ATR ('the Turtle N'). Pyramiding: add another Unit every +1/2 N of favorable move, up to a max of 4-5 Units, raising the stop on the whole stack with each add. Initial stop = 2N below the entry of each unit (so ~2% account risk if fully sized; ~1% per unit). The whole apparatus is volatility-normalized so every market risks the same fraction of equity.
ws4_methods.exit: No fixed profit target — this is the defining feature. Exit is itself a Donchian channel: System 1 exits a long on a 10-day low (close below the lowest low of prior 10 days); System 2 exits on a 20-day low. The 2N initial stop protects new/losing trades; once a trade runs, the channel-low trailing exit takes over and can hold a winner for weeks to months. So the bracket is: hard 2N stop on entry, opposing-channel trailing exit for winners, no take-profit. Losers are cut at 2N (small, fast); winners ride until the trend breaks the opposing channel.
ws4_methods.how_to_test_here: We already have the machinery to test the SHELL of this cheaply, and an important in-house prior. (1) Indicator exists: `calculate_donchian(window)` in src/bluehorseshoe/analysis/indicators/trend_indicators.py returns +2 when close > shifted upper band (a 20-day breakout) and is registered in get_score() under DONCHIAN_MULTIPLIER. So a breakout-gated long candidate set is already producible via the normal -p scorer path. (2) Backtester (src/bluehorseshoe/analysis/backtest.py) supports next-day fill, ATR-based stop, hold_days cap, and use_trailing_stop with trailing_multiplier (ATR units) — this is the closest analog to the 2N-stop + trailing exit. (3) Concrete test: build a hypothetical-trade set over the DuckDB store (1999-present) where entry = bar after a fresh 20-day-high breakout (close > prior 20d high) among names passing price $5-$500 / vol >100k, with an optional price>200d-MA long filter; stop = entry - 2*ATR(20); exit = trailing ATR stop OR opposing 10-day-low close, and feed through the hypothetical-trade evaluator. CRITICAL: run it BOTH with our standard 5-10d hold cap AND with hold_days effectively uncapped (e.g. 60-120d) — the cap is the make-or-break variable, because the Turtle edge is entirely in the long-hold right tail. Also test a 1:1 fixed-target variant for direct comparison. Prior result to respect: docs/planning/DONCHIAN_STRATEGY_v1.md is a clean NULL for Donchian breakouts in the FTMO H4 universe at fixed 1:1 RR across mid/limit/stop entries — and it explicitly found that 'take quick wins' (1:1) dominated 'let winners run' (1:2, 1:3) THERE because that universe was range-bound. That finding does not transfer directly to US equities (different asset, longer trends, daily bars), but it is a strong caution that breakout shapes underperform mean-reversion in our tested universes when winners are not allowed to run.

ws4_methods.core_idea: A price "gap" is when today's open prints materially away from the prior session's close (a window left on the chart). The methodology has two opposite playbooks. GAP-AND-GO (continuation): a stock gaps UP on a catalyst (earnings, news, sector rotation) and you bet the gap is the start of a move, buying in the direction of the gap when it shows it will "go" rather than fade. GAP-FADE (reversal/fill): you bet the gap is an overreaction that mean-reverts toward the prior close ("filling the gap"), fading the move. Practitioners classify gaps as breakaway (start of trend, gap-and-go), continuation/runaway (mid-trend, go), exhaustion (end of trend, fade), and common/area (low-conviction, usually fills/fade). Edge claims: full gaps in liquid names that hold the opening range tend to continue intraday-to-multiday; small/common gaps into resistance tend to fill. Confirmation tools used: relative volume on the gap bar (high RVOL = real catalyst = go; low RVOL = noise = fade), the opening range / first-bar hold, prior trend context (gap in trend direction = continuation), and proximity to prior support/resistance.
ws4_methods.selection: Daily-bar adaptation of selection: (1) compute overnight gap pct = today_open / prior_close - 1; flag setups where |gap| exceeds a threshold (e.g. >2-4% up for gap-and-go, or a smaller 1-3% common gap for the fade). (2) Confirm with relative volume on the gap day (RVOL > ~1.5x 20-day avg is the catalyst proxy — we already have calculate_rvol). (3) Context filters: gap-and-go wants the gap aligned with an existing uptrend (above rising 20/50 EMA, ADX up) and clearing prior resistance/Donchian high; gap-fade wants an overextended gap into a level (RSI/BB stretch, gap into prior resistance with weak RVOL). (4) Apply our universe gates: price $5-$500, avg vol >100k, long-biased so gap-and-go on up-gaps is the primary track; down-gap fades (buying the fill) are the long-biased fade variant. Practitioners traditionally also use float, short interest, and news quality — none of which we have.
ws4_methods.entry: Practitioner (intraday) entry is the load-bearing part and is where the methodology breaks against us: gap-and-go enters on the break of the first 1-5 min opening-range high (ORB) after the gap holds; gap-fade enters on a failed push / first pullback intraday. With DAILY bars we cannot see the opening range at all — we only have one open and one close per day. Our forced approximation: signal fires on the close of the gap day (or the prior close, treating the gap-day open as the trigger), and we enter on the NEXT day using our standard bracket evaluator (entry = a limit at/near the prior close-ish level, filled when next-day low crosses it; check_entry already models open-gap-through fills). This converts an intraday momentum play into a 1-bar-delayed daily swing entry — a fundamentally different, weaker instrument than the real setup.
ws4_methods.exit: Daily-bar exit fits our existing machinery cleanly: ATR-based bracket — stop below the gap-day low (gap-and-go) or beyond the gap origin, target sized to keep risk:reward > 1.0, hold horizon capped at 5-10 trading days via the trade_evaluator hold_days param (intrabar stop/target priority already implemented, MAE/MFE tracked). For the fade, the natural target is the gap fill (prior close) with a stop beyond the gap extreme. The real intraday method exits same-day on VWAP loss or ORB failure — we cannot replicate that, so our version holds overnight, which raises gap-risk and changes the edge profile.
ws4_methods.how_to_test_here: Fully testable in-stack as a daily-bar approximation without writing new infra: (1) Add a gap feature in a new indicator or inline: gap_pct = open / close.shift(1) - 1, plus a gap-into-prior-extreme flag, computed straight from the DuckDB ohlcv table (open/high/low/close/volume all present; confirmed in duckdb_store.py). (2) Reuse calculate_rvol (volume_indicators.py) for the catalyst proxy. (3) Define two candidate generators: gap_and_go (up-gap > X% AND RVOL > Y AND above rising EMA/Donchian breakout) and gap_fade_long (down-gap into support, low RVOL, target = gap fill). (4) Evaluate with the existing Backtester (backtest.py) / TradeEvalConfig+check_entry in trade_evaluator.py over the 1999-present DuckDB universe: entry next bar via the bracket, hold_days=5-10, ATR stop, RR>1.0, measure win rate, mean R, MAE/MFE, and crucially compare gap-day-open-to-close behavior to confirm whether any edge survives once you can only act on the daily close. (5) Sweep gap thresholds, RVOL thresholds, and up vs down gaps as a grid (mirrors the bh_ftmo per-cell sweep methodology). Key diagnostic: measure how much of the cited edge lives in the first intraday hour (unobservable to us) vs the close-to-close move (the only thing we can trade) — if the edge is intraday-only, reject.

ws4_methods.core_idea: Buy temporary weakness inside an established uptrend rather than chasing breakouts. The premise: in a healthy trend, price oscillates around a short-term moving average (the 10 or 20 EMA acts as a "dynamic support" / value zone). A pullback to that MA is a lower-risk re-entry into a move that is statistically likely to continue. The edge is behavioral/structural: trend-followers and momentum funds re-add on dips, and the tight MA gives an objective, repeatable place to define risk. It is the long-biased trend-continuation cousin of mean reversion: it fades the small counter-move, but only in the direction of the dominant trend (so it is NOT bottom-fishing a downtrend).
ws4_methods.selection: Practitioners gate on regime first, then setup. (1) TREND FILTER: stock must be in a confirmed uptrend, typically price above a rising 50-EMA and 200-EMA (or 50>200 "golden" alignment), and the 10-EMA above the 20-EMA. ADX>20-25 is often added to require an actual trend (not chop). (2) PULLBACK: price retraces to "touch" or close near the 10 or 20 EMA — measured as low piercing the MA, or close within ~0.5-1.0 ATR of it — typically after 2-4 down/sideways bars, ideally with declining volume on the pullback (orderly profit-taking, not distribution). (3) The pullback must NOT break market structure: it should hold above the prior swing low and stay above the 50-EMA. (4) Often a confirmation trigger is required: a bullish reversal candle at the MA (hammer/engulfing) or the first up-bar that takes out the prior bar's high. Universe is liquid trending names; many run it on the strongest RS stocks in an up-market.
ws4_methods.entry: Buy-stop above the high of the reversal/confirmation bar at the MA (entry on the bar that resumes the trend), OR a limit buy at/just above the 10/20 EMA for the more aggressive "anticipation" version. Most disciplined practitioners use the stop-entry (confirmation) variant to avoid buying a pullback that keeps falling.
ws4_methods.exit: Stop-loss just below the pullback swing low or below the 20-EMA, commonly sized at ~1-1.5 ATR (this defines the R). Targets: (a) fixed R-multiple (1.5R-3R), (b) a measured-move / prior swing high, or (c) trail under the rising 10/20 EMA (or chandelier ATR trail) to ride the continuation. Time-stop: exit if the trade hasn't resolved within N bars (the pullback is supposed to resolve quickly; a stalling trade invalidates the thesis). Because the stop is tight against the MA and the target is a continuation leg, R:R is naturally >1.

(1) EMAs are already computed in moving_average_indicators.py (9/21/50/200 EMAs via .ewm()); add/confirm a 10 and 20 EMA. ADX/DMI exists in trend_indicators.py (calculate_dmi_adx), and ATR exists (ATR_WINDOW=14) for stop sizing. ws4_methods.core_idea: Richard Wyckoff's accumulation schematic models how "composite operators" absorb supply inside a sideways trading range (TR) before a markup. The range is bounded by Support (the Selling-Climax low) and Resistance (the Automatic-Rally top). The named events: SC (selling climax) > AR (automatic rally) > ST (secondary test) > a contracting series of swings, then the SPRING (Shakeout): price stabs BELOW range support on relatively HIGH volume to trip stops and grab the last supply, then snaps back ABOVE support, closing back inside the range — proving demand has overcome supply. After the spring, a Test (a low-volume retest that holds higher) marks the Last Point of Support (LPS), and the Sign of Strength (SOS) rally on expanding volume confirms markup. The "re-entry" variant traded here is NOT the spring stab itself but the LPS/SOS re-entry: wait for the spring to validate, then buy the higher-low pullback (LPS) or the backup after the breakout above range resistance/AR ("jump the creek, back up to the creek"). The method is a demand-vs-supply read driven primarily by PRICE STRUCTURE inside a horizontal range plus VOLUME behavior at the edges (contraction into the range, high volume on the shakeout, expanding volume on the markup, no-supply/no-demand bars on pullbacks).
ws4_methods.selection: Universe filter for names in a multi-week horizontal trading range (base/consolidation). Practitioners screen for: (1) a prior down-leg or sideways drift into a basing range; (2) defined horizontal support and resistance — range high/low roughly flat over N weeks (e.g. 20-60 sessions), i.e. low ATR-normalized range width and near-zero regression slope; (3) volatility/range CONTRACTION as the range matures (declining ATR and declining volume — supply drying up); (4) a SPRING = a session whose low pierces the established range support (rolling N-day min) but closes back above it, ideally on elevated volume, followed by a successful low-volume Test that holds above the spring low. Candidates ranked by how textbook the structure is (clean flat range, decisive spring recovery, volume confirmation, higher-low LPS). Long-biased by construction (accumulation = bottoming). Market/sector context is a soft overlay (Wyckoff read the broad market first).
ws4_methods.entry: Two practitioner styles, both daily-bar compatible. (A) LPS / spring-test entry: after the spring bar closes back inside the range, enter on the retest pullback that makes a HIGHER low than the spring low — typically a stop-buy above the test bar's high, or a limit near the test low. Earlier, tighter stop. (B) SOS / creek-jump entry: wait for a breakout CLOSE above range resistance (or above the AR) on expanding volume, then enter on the low-volume backup toward the broken resistance (now support). Later, higher-probability. Confirmation gates: spring low held on the test, volume expansion on up-legs, no-supply (low-volume down) bars on pullbacks.
ws4_methods.exit: Stop: just below the SPRING low — the structural invalidation; a close back under the spring low says accumulation failed. Tight and well-defined because the spring low is a recent extreme. Target: measured-move / range objective — classically a point-and-figure count across the range, in practice the range height projected up from the breakout, or the next overhead supply shelf. R:R is naturally >1 entering near range support against a target at/above range top. Time stop: exit if markup fails to develop within a defined window. Fits the 5-10 day swing horizon ONLY if sized to the small LPS-to-range-top leg; the full Wyckoff campaign (spring through markup) typically runs weeks, which is the main horizon mismatch.
ws4_methods.how_to_test_here: Build a deterministic rules-based "Wyckoff spring re-entry" detector as a new scorer/signal — pure price/volume, no fundamentals/intraday. (1) RANGE detection over lookback W (sweep 20/30/40/60): support=rolling min(low,W), resistance=rolling max(high,W); require ATR-normalized width below a threshold AND near-zero linear-reg slope to confirm a flat base. (2) CONTRACTION gate: ATR(14) and avg volume declining over the back half of W. (3) SPRING bar: low[t] < prior_support AND close[t] > prior_support (pierce-and-recover) with volume confirmation via existing src/bluehorseshoe/analysis/indicators/volume_indicators.py — RVOL spike (calculate_rvol) and/or MFI/CMF turning up. (4) RE-ENTRY trigger: next bar(s) make a higher low (style A LPS) or close above resistance then pull back (style B SOS). Emit a bracket: entry=trigger price, stop=spring_low*0.99, target=entry+(resistance-support), capped so R:R>1.0 and risk<=5% (constants.py MAX_RISK_PERCENT); apply $5-$500 / avg-vol>100k filters. Feed brackets into Backtester.evaluate_prediction (src/bluehorseshoe/analysis/backtest.py) over the DuckDB store (1999-present, ~11k symbols) — it already accepts entry/stop/target + hold_days. Test two horizons: hold_days~10 (style A small leg, our native swing window) AND a 30-40 day cap (full campaign) to locate where the edge lives. Report per-trade R, win rate, realized vs structural R:R, segmented by spring-volume-confirmed vs not — the volume gate is the falsifiable core of the hypothesis. Rolling min/max + slope are trivial additions alongside existing indicators.
